 BTS kicks off Asia-Pacific leg of ‘Arirang’ world tour in Kaohsiung
 Published : Nov. 19, 2026 - 17:21:30
 Add The Korea Herald on Google
 Link copied!
 Lee Jung-joo 
Covering K-pop issues, trends
 Subscribe + 
 Landmarks in Kaohsiung, Taiwan, are illuminated in purple ahead of BTS' scheduled concerts in the city on Thursday, Saturday and Sunday. (@Btsworld62953 on X) BTS begins the Asia-Pacific leg of its “Arirang” world tour in Kaohsiung, Taiwan, on Thursday, continuing a global trek that has already taken the group across North America, Europe and South America.
 The group is set to perform at Kaohsiung National Stadium on Thursday, Saturday and Sunday, before heading to Bangkok; Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia; Singapore, Jakarta, Indonesia; Hong Kong and Bulacan, the Philippines.
 Across Asia, BTS will stage 21 concerts in seven cities, followed by five additional shows in Melbourne and Sydney in February 2027, bringing the Asia-Pacific leg to 26 performances across nine cities.
 Kaohsiung has rolled out a series of citywide programs around the concerts, with landmarks including 85 Sky Tower, Love River, Great Harbor Bridge and Kaohsiung Music Center illuminated in purple, a signature color long associated with the group and its fandom, known as Army.
 Other programs planned during the concert period in Taiwan include a music fountain show along Love River and K-pop random play dance events across the city.
 The city has also introduced transportation and tourism measures aimed at concertgoers. A “Bus 613” shuttle service — referencing BTS’ June 13 debut date — will operate during the concerts, while selected pedestrian signals around the city feature messages such as “Army Stop” and “Army Go.”
 Pedestrian signals in Kaohsiung, Taiwan, show "Army Stop" and "Army Go" in celebration of BTS' scheduled concerts in the city on Thursday, Saturday and Sunday. (@Ceolmh3 on X) A BTS-themed photo zone has also been installed at Kaohsiung International Airport, while welcome messages are displayed on subway gates.
 The concerts will also reach audiences outside Taiwan through live viewing screenings. BTS’ Kaohsiung show on Saturday and the Jakarta concert on Dec. 29 will be screened in theaters across more than 80 countries and regions, either live or on a delayed basis, depending on time zone.
 The Kaohsiung concert is expected to be shown on roughly 3,300 screens worldwide, while the Jakarta show will reach around 2,800 screens.
 BTS performs on the "Arirang" tour at Morumbi Stadium in Sao Paulo, Brazil, where the group had shows on Oct. 28, 30 and 31. (Big Hit Music) The tour will later move to Singapore, where BTS will perform four shows at the National Stadium on Dec. 17, 19, 20 and 22. The concerts will coincide with “The City Arirang,” a monthlong citywide project running from Dec. 1 to 31 in collaboration with the Singapore Tourism Board.
 Programs will include a light and music show at Jewel Changi Airport, a drone show involving 1,500 drones on the resort island Sentosa, as well as red illuminations across landmarks near Marina Bay, including the Merlion, Singapore Flyer and Fullerton Hotel.
 BTS’ citywide project, which began in Seoul in March, expanded to Las Vegas, Busan, London and New York before arriving in the southeast Asian city. The edition in Singapore will be its longest-running edition so far, spanning the entire month of December.
 Meanwhile, BTS emerged as the biggest winner at the 2026 Melon Music Awards on Saturday and Sunday, taking home six trophies, including the grand prizes for artist of the year and album of the year for “Arirang” as well as best male group and stage of the year.
 BTS also earned five group nominations for the upcoming MAMA Awards to be held Friday and Saturday, including artist of the year, album of the year, best male group, best vocal performance group and best music video.
